title: How to Identify (and Stop) Those Pesky Car Extended Warranty Calls
summary: A consumer-tech explainer lays out how car warranty phone scams work, the tells that identify them, where scammers get personal data, and how to stop and verify such calls.

assertions.quote: Scam callers almost always try to instill a sense of urgency in their victims
car warranty scams occur when someone poses as a representative of an insurer, manufacturer or car dealership
a company needs your direct permission to call you if it's trying to sell something

verdicts.note: TCPA rules require prior express consent for autodialed or prerecorded sales calls, making unconsented robocalls illegal, a well-established legal fact.

The data book confirms the general legal rule that a sales robocall requires the recipient's prior written permission regardless of Registry status, and separately tracks 'Warranties & protection plans' as a complaint category split almost evenly between live-caller and robocall complaints in FY2025 (10,813 vs 10,503), confirming warranty-related robocalls are a real, measured share of complaints.

assertions.quote: Companies will never call you to have you verify your identity or provide sensitive personal information over the phone

verdicts.note: Many legitimate companies do verify identity on calls the customer initiated, but on an unsolicited inbound call from an unknown party, giving out SSNs or account numbers is reliably unsafe.

assertions.quote: the number may appear to be from a certain area code (usually local), but the call did not actually originate from the number

verdicts.note: Caller ID spoofing of local numbers ('neighbor spoofing') is a well-documented and common robocall technique confirmed by the FCC.

assertions.quote: this list helps block telemarketing calls, not scam calls.

verdicts.note: The registry only binds telemarketers complying with the law; outright scammers already breaking the law aren't deterred by it, as the FTC itself notes.

FTC's registry data book states telemarketers and sellers must remove registered numbers from their call lists at least every 31 days (reducing legitimate sales calls), while sales robocalls are illegal whether or not a number is registered unless the caller has written permission -- and FY2025 data show registrations still climbing while robocalls, not calls from registered legitimate telemarketers, drive most complaint volume.

assertions.quote: the information can also come from legitimate sources like a state department of motor vehicles
the safest and most reliable way to avoid car warranty fraud is to check directly with your vehicle's manufacturer or the dealership

verdicts.note: Contacting a known, independently looked-up source rather than a number provided by the caller is standard anti-fraud verification practice.
